title: Backend selection and compute provenance
text: Use device = "cpu" reproducible portable execution matters automatic hardware selection. Every returned cudatensor records actual stage: provenance table one row per stage: requested_device caller’s policy ("cpu", "cuda", "auto", "fixed-cpu", "inherited"); device stage actually computed; backend names implementation, base torch; selection_reason explains resolution; fallback true automatic request selected CPU; output_device stage placed result. infer output location device. transfer hybrid operation can compute one device return data another.
code: left_source <- matrix(   1:6,   nrow = 2,   dimnames = list(     sample = c("sample_a", "sample_b"),     feature = c("gene_a", "gene_b", "gene_c")   ) ) right_source <- matrix(   seq_len(6) / 10,   nrow = 3,   dimnames = list(     feature = c("gene_a", "gene_b", "gene_c"),     component = c("component_1", "component_2")   ) )  left <- cuda_tensor(left_source, device = "cpu", dtype = "float64") right <- cuda_tensor(right_source, device = "cpu", dtype = "float64") product <- tensor_matmul(left, right)  tensor_device(product) #>  device backend  #>   "cpu"  "base" to_cpu(product) #>           component #> sample     component_1 component_2 #>   sample_a         2.2         4.9 #>   sample_b         2.8         6.4 construction_provenance <- cuda_provenance(left) construction_provenance #> <cuda_provenance schema=cudaverse-stage/1 stages=1 compute=cpu> #>                   stage requested_device device backend selection_reason #>  tensor_materialization              cpu    cpu    base     explicit_cpu #>  fallback output_device #>     FALSE           cpu  product_provenance <- cuda_provenance(product) product_provenance #> <cuda_provenance schema=cudaverse-stage/1 stages=1 compute=cpu> #>            stage requested_device device backend selection_reason fallback #>  matrix_multiply        inherited    cpu    base inherited_device    FALSE #>  output_device #>            cpu  attr(product_provenance, "schema") #> [1] "cudaverse-stage/1" attr(product_provenance, "compute_device") #> [1] "cpu"

title: Backend selection and compute provenance
text: Dense cudaverse tensors use dense storage. payload alone approximately prod(shape) * bytes_per_value, outputs temporary tensors. CPU fallback uses ordinary R vectors, physical storage differs torch: CPU float32 values rounded IEEE single precision stored public operation, base R kernels accumulate double precision. CUDA kernels compute native torch dtype. Results therefore compared explicit tolerance rather expected bit--bit identical. Floating tensors may contain IEEE Inf, -Inf, NaN; integer tensors reject values represented exactly. Creating CUDA tensor R object transfers dense input host memory GPU memory. to_cpu(), .array(), .matrix() materialize complete result host memory. Mixed-device binary operations move right operand left operand’s device. CUDA subsetting replacement currently make CPU round trip; matrix arithmetic, broadcasting, reductions, reshape, transpose use tensor’s backend. Large operations can temporarily require input, output, intermediate allocations . package currently provide --core execution automatic chunking. Printing tensor 100 values shows metadata without copying full CUDA allocation; explicitly call to_cpu() transfer intended.

title: cudaverse 0.1.0
text: Establishes one user-facing package general-purpose cudaverse API. Incorporates dense tensor functionality cudatensr. Incorporates sparse matrix functionality cudasparsr. Incorporates numerical algorithms cudalearnr. Incorporates graph workflows cudagraphR. Incorporates embedding workflows cudaembedr. Preserves canonical cuda_provenance() protocol across modules. Keeps single-cell-specific workflows separate cudacellr package. Fixes CUDA indexing, R column-major reshape semantics, exact self-distance diagonals compatibility R torch 0.17. Documents measured, benchmark-gated roadmap toward lightweight native CUDA backend retaining current portable CPU fallback.
